textbookText: 10.8 Force Set-Up Due to Expansion or Contraction and Thermal Stress
If a metal bar is heated it will expand, but if we prevent it from
expanding then large forces will be set up within the bar. The force
will be that which would be needed to compress the bar to its original length from the expanded position. This force is called
force set up due to expansion. Similarly, if a metallic wire tied
between two rigid poles is cooled, it will try to contract but will
not be able to do so because of rigid poles. Instead, a large force
is set up to prevent the phenomenon of contraction. This force is [Fig;10.10 Force set up due to expansion] called force set up due to contraction.
The mechanical force that occurs in an object when it is prevented either from expansion during heating or from contraction during cooling is called force set-up due to expansion or contraction.
Mathematically, it is given by F = YA   ; where Y= Young’s Modulus of elasticity, A= cross-sectional area,  = thermal strain. The stress corresponding to this force is called Thermal stress.
